correctness.rationale: From the finite irreducible birth–death rates, detailed balance yields pi(k) proportional to binom(S,k)[(Z)_k(Z)_(S-k)]^q, a known Mobilia formula. The adjacent ratio of the quotient pi2/pi1 on the left half has logarithm q1*ln[(a1+d)/(a1-d)] - q2*ln[(a2+d)/(a2-d)], where a_i=(S-1)/2+Z_i and d=(S-1)/2-k. Each log equals integral_0^d 2a/(a^2-t^2)dt; the kernel ratio is strictly increasing, making F(d) a strictly increasing weighted mean for 0<d<=m<a1<a2. Allowed d run from m down to d_min (1/2 even S, 1 odd S), so the sign pattern yields exact two endpoint thresholds and a unique possible interior likelihood maximum. Reflection matches radial masses; monotone likelihood ratios imply strict tail comparisons; averaging convex test functions over symmetric K pairs gives convex orders. Independent exact integer sign grid and S=20 q2=6,7,8 regimes corroborate, but do not establish the universal integral monotonicity.

originality.rationale: Mobilia (2015) supplies exactly the same birth–death mechanism and stationary distribution (Eq. 10) and discusses modality as parameters vary. The original formula is not claimed new. Its inspected Sections II/IV do not state the two-control sharp likelihood-ratio thresholds, nonmonotone relative-likelihood middle interval, or strict convex-order consequences. Mellor–Mobilia–Zia (2016) treat heterogeneous consultation classes with different state space, not this same S across two models. Priority remains qualified for generic monotone likelihood ratio comparative-statics theorems.
